the induction of NAG- 1 by DADS in HCT-116 colorectal cancer cells is mediated by a p53- dependent pathway.
the antitumorgenic and apoptosis-inducing effects of DADS in human colon cancer HCT-116 and prostate cancer PC-3 cells are dependent on p53 and NAC-1, respectively.
Diallyl disulphide (DADS), a constituent of garlic, induces apoptosis and upregulates NAG-1 (a pro-apoptotic gene) in human colon cancer cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the molecular mechanisms by which DADS induces the antitumor protein NAG-1 and apoptosis in human colorectal cancer cells.
the induction of apoptosis in human colorectal cancer cells by DADS, a component of garlic.
the ability of DADS to induce apoptosis in colorectal and prostate cancer cell lines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DADS induces apoptosis and NAG protein in HCT-116 wild-type p53 cells via a p53-dependent pathway.
DADS induces apoptosis and NAG protein expression via a p53-dependent pathway in human colorectal cancer HCT 116 (wild-type) cells.
DADS induced NAG-1 and apoptosis in HCT-116 p53+/+ human colorectal cancer cells, but not in HCT-115 p53-/- human colorectal cancer or in PC-3 human prostate cancer cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DADS induced apoptosis and NAG protein in HCT-116, but not in HCT- 15 or PC-3 cells, and the induction was mediated through p53.
DADS induces NAG-1 via p53 in HCT-116 and that this is one mechanism by which DADS induces apoptosis in these cells.
DADS is an anticancer agent that induces NAG-1 and p53 in wild-type p53 cells and apoptosis in HCT-116, HCT-15, and PC-3 cell lines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DADS induces NAG-1 and apoptosis in human colorectal cancer cells in a p53-dependent manner.
DADS induces apoptosis in human cancer cells by a p53-mediated mechanism.
DADS is able to induce NAG- and apoptosis-related genes in human colorectal and prostate cancer cells and may serve as a chemopreventive agent against colon and prostate cancer.
